title: §.XIII: Reformed not self-hostile — Neostadian note that AC is not Scripture; Calovius unfair
pass_a_gloss: Nor are the Reformed here hostile to themselves, when with the Neostadian Theologians in Cap. IV from p. 143 concerning the Augsburg Confession they note against those who go nearly to equate it with Sacred Scripture (which Calovius, unfairly indeed and not except by insult, interprets as Calvinian insults, Crit. Sacr. p. 68.) That it was written not so many years after the beginning of the Reformation, in which not so suddenly could all things be seen through and explained, &c. &c.
pass_b_english: Nor are the Reformed here their own enemies when, with the Neustadt theologians (Cap. IV from p. 143) on the Augsburg Confession, they note against those who nearly equate it with Holy Scripture — which Calovius unfairly, and only by insult, reads as "Calvinian insults" (Crit. Sacr. p. 68).
They note that it was written not many years after the Reformation began, when not everything could suddenly be seen through and explained, and so on.
source_text: Neque hîc sibi ipsis infesti sunt Reformati, quando cum Neostadianis Theologis Cap. IV. à pag. 143. de Augustana Confessione, contra hos, qui eam, tantum non Sacrae Scripturae aequiparatum eunt, annotant (id quod Calovius, iniquè profectò & non nisi per convitium, Calviniana convitia interpretatur, Crit. Sacr. pag. 68.) Esse eam scriptam annis non ita multis post Reformationis initium, in quo non tam subitò potuerunt omnia perspici & explicari &c. &c.
